transcript.content: Hello, and welcome. I'm Dr. [Name], a psychiatrist here. What brings you in to see me today?

My family made me come. They... they keep saying the bank papers prove nothing was taken. But I know they're hiding my money. It's been over a year. They use bills and... fundraisers, trip plans... just to cover it up. I have to keep confronting them until they tell the truth.

Over the past year while you've been dealing with this situation about your money, how has your mood been? Have you been feeling unusually energetic, needing less sleep, or feeling unusually happy or irritable?
I don't know. My mood is just... regular. I sleep fine. I'm not unusually happy or anything, no. Not with what they're doing. I'm just normal.
When you think about your family hiding your money, do you have a clear, detailed understanding of exactly how they're doing it and why, or does it sometimes feel unclear or confusing to you?
I don't... I don't know all the details. I just know they have it. I don't really get how they do all the bank stuff, or the papers. They just do it.
Have you ever heard voices or seen things that other people around you couldn't hear or see, especially related to your family or the money situation?
No. I don't... hear voices. Or see things. Just... no. I don't have that.
Besides your family, do you think anyone else—like people at the bank, the government, or strangers—might be involved in taking your money or helping your family hide it?
I don't think so. Just... just them. I don't know about any bank people or strangers. It's just my family.

If your family showed you all the bank records and a complete accounting, would you be able to accept that your money is actually there and safe, or do you think they would have faked those documents too?

They... they already do that. My family and friends, they keep saying the bank papers prove nothing was taken. But... I know they're hiding it. It's been over a year. 

They just use things to cover it up. Like... bills. Or fundraisers. Trip plans. It's all just to hide where the money went. 

So... no. I won't just accept it. I have to keep confronting them. Just... until they finally tell the truth.
When you think about how your family is hiding your money, can you walk me through the steps—like, what exactly do they do first, then second, then third? How does the whole plan work?

I don't... I don't know all the steps. I just know it's gone. 

They do things. I don't know the exact order. They just... they take it. And then they make up reasons. I don't know how the whole plan works. I just know what they're doing.
Is there any possibility at all that you could be mistaken about your family taking your money, or are you completely certain that this is what happened?

No. I'm not mistaken. 

I know what I know. It's been over a year. They keep showing me those bank papers, saying they prove nothing was taken... but I know they're lying. They're hiding it. They use the bills... the fundraisers... the trips. It's all a cover-up. 

I'm certain. I just... I have to keep confronting them until they tell the truth.

If someone you completely trusted—like a therapist or doctor—reviewed all your bank records with you and explained everything in detail, do you think you might consider the possibility that your money is actually safe, or is there no way you could ever believe that?

I... no. I already told you. 

The papers don't mean anything. Even if you or someone else looks at them... it doesn't change what I know. My family and friends keep saying those papers prove it's all there, but... they're just lying. They've been hiding it for over a year. 

A doctor looking at the papers won't change that they're using bills and... and trip plans to cover it up. So... no. I wouldn't believe it. I just have to keep confronting them. That's all I can do.

latest_inference.note: Patient demonstrates fixed, false belief about family stealing money that persists despite contradictory evidence (bank records). Refuses to consider alternative explanations even with authority figures. No hallucinations, normal mood, no thought disorder. Belief is circumscribed to one theme. This is consistent with Delusional Disorder, Erotomanic type would involve romantic themes (ruled out). Persecutory type involves beliefs of being harmed/conspired against (partially fits but primary concern is theft). Somatic type involves body concerns (ruled out). Grandiose type involves inflated self-esteem (ruled out). Mixed type possible but the theft theme dominates. F22.0 (Delusional Disorder, Paranoid Type) best fits the persistent, non-bizarre delusion of reference and persecution through theft by known individuals.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient presents with a non-bizarre delusional belief (money being hidden by family) that has persisted for over one year without prominent hallucinations, mood disturbance, or significant cognitive decline. The belief is fixed and resistant to contradictory evidence (bank records), meeting criteria for delusional disorder, somatic type (F22.0).
